I am a woman with small hands to feed, and this sorghum plot is only a small piece of my land. I keep some cattle, so I carry their manure to the field because it costs me nothing but my back. Chemical fertilizer from the cooperative is dear, and the rains in Amhara can fail — I dare not borrow money for DAP and urea on such a small plot, so I use just a little if the development agent brings some on credit. I plant the sorghum seed I saved from last harvest, intercropped with a bit of haricot bean, and my children and I weed it by hand; I have no money to hire people.
